comment: Independent source-first review of the three configured model-condition rows. These rows make ordinary meaning conditions for the source probability model visible: measurability of reported probabilities, the user-approved event-calibration reading of the point-fiber display, and integrability of the strategy correctness indicator. They are not proof conclusions and are not inferred from their declaration names.

∀ i : Fin n, ∀ A : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet.reason: This is the expanded event-calibration identity used by the raw joint-law model. It gives the source display a total meaning without asserting a chosen pointwise conditional probability on zero-probability prediction fibers.

premises: ∀ i : Fin n, ∀ A : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet A → E[1_{P_i(X) ∈ A,Y=1}] = E[P_i(X) 1_{P_i(X) ∈ A}]
source_assumption_event_calibration.reason: The source requires calibrated predictors. Its point-fiber conditional display does not select a conditional value on a null fiber, so the reviewed model uses the explicitly documented, user-approved event identity for every measurable set of reported probabilities. This is a calibration reading of the source model, not an extra conclusion used to prove the theorem.
source_assumption_event_calibration.validator: Codex PKG25 independent semantic assumption audit 2026-07-24

∀ i : Fin n, Measurable (S.pred i).reason: This is the expanded measurable-random-variable condition needed to interpret P_i(X), its measurable reported-value events, and the source expectation notation on an arbitrary measurable input space.

source_assumption_predictor_measurabilit.reason: The source forms random reported probabilities, conditions on reported-probability events, and takes expectations under an arbitrary distribution. The unfolded condition requires each predictor P_i to be measurable, which is the standard model-definedness condition for those expressions; it neither changes the reliability conclusion nor supplies an adversarial-witness fact.

source_assumption_strategy_expectation_w.reason: The source defines an arbitrary deterministic strategy and then calls its expected binary correctness an accuracy. Predictor measurability alone does not make that induced indicator integrable on an arbitrary measurable space, so the unfolded condition is the analytic definedness condition for the displayed expectation. It is discharged by the finite witnesses and does not assert a substantive property of a strategy's output.
